scout.purpose: Android components are system entry points with different lifecycle and visibility contracts; choosing by habit leads to restricted, wasteful, or unsafe work.
scout.realWorldUse: Activities host UI, services support ongoing work, receivers handle brief broadcasts, and providers expose structured data across process boundaries.
scout.outcome: Choose a component from the job contract, explain service threading and foreground obligations, and prefer task-specific background APIs when suitable.

sections.title: Components are entry points, not architecture layers

blocks.text: An Activity presents an interactive UI. A Service has no UI and can represent started or bound ongoing work. A BroadcastReceiver handles a short delivered event. A ContentProvider offers a URI-based structured data interface, often across applications. The Application instance is process setup rather than one of the four primary externally activated component types. Components are created by the system and declared or registered under platform rules. Domain models and repositories should not become component subclasses merely to gain Context. Select a component only when the system needs that entry/lifecycle contract.

blocks.title: Component contract
rows: Ongoing or client-bound operation without UI
Brief response to a broadcast event

blocks.caption: The manifest lets Android discover component classes and their exposure contract.

sections.title: A Service does not provide a worker thread

blocks.text: A started service receives start requests and remains until stopped or the system applies lifecycle rules. A bound service exposes a client interface while bindings exist. Both run on the application main thread by default, so blocking work still needs asynchronous execution. Background execution limits make an ordinary background service inappropriate for most deferred work. WorkManager is generally better for guaranteed deferrable work; media, navigation, active device communication, or another user-noticeable ongoing task may justify a foreground service. Match the API to urgency, user visibility, duration, and interruption semantics.

blocks.caption: The service callback coordinates work but does not turn the main thread into a background thread.

steps.label: User-noticeable now?
steps.detail: Consider a correctly typed foreground service.

sections.title: Foreground services require continuous user awareness

blocks.text: A foreground service performs an ongoing operation noticeable to the user and displays a notification. It must declare appropriate service types and permissions, promote itself promptly after a permitted start, and stop when the user-visible work ends. Modern Android restricts starting foreground services from the background, with narrow exemptions. While-in-use permissions can further constrain camera, microphone, or location service starts. A foreground service is not a loophole for unrestricted background execution or a way to make a process immortal. Design interruption, notification actions, restart policy, and persisted recovery data explicitly.

blocks.caption: Starting and promotion are separate obligations, and current platform restrictions determine whether the start is permitted.

blocks.title: User-visible means genuinely noticeable
blocks.text: If the work does not deserve an ongoing notification, a foreground service is probably the wrong API.

inspect.title: Choose an API for note backup
inspect.code: Requirement: upload local notes eventually when network is available; user need not watch; retry across app restart.
walkthrough: The work is deferrable rather than continuously user-noticeable.
It needs constraints, retry, and durable scheduling.
A foreground service notification would misrepresent background maintenance.
inspect.expectedOutput: Use WorkManager rather than a plain or foreground service.

trap_check.why: Service callbacks run on the application main thread by default.
trap_check.fix: Use asynchronous work and choose an API that matches the job contract.

trap_check.mistake: Using a foreground service for silent maintenance.
trap_check.why: It violates the user-noticeable contract and encounters platform restrictions.
trap_check.fix: Use WorkManager or a task-specific background API.

challenge_intro.task: Classify audio-note playback, local backup, a short boot event, and cross-app note query into appropriate components or APIs with lifecycle and failure reasoning.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Every choice names urgency, visibility, duration, and retry needs. No Service is assumed to provide a worker thread. Foreground service choices include notification and stop behaviour.

recall.prompt: What is a Service missing by design?
recall.answer: A user interface and an automatic worker thread.

recall.prompt: When is a foreground service appropriate?
recall.answer: For ongoing work genuinely noticeable to the user and permitted by platform rules.
WorkManager normally models constraints, retry, and durable scheduling.

objectives: Select Android components by system contract.
Explain started/bound service lifecycle and threading.
Reserve foreground services for permitted user-visible work.
